73.s: Which cycle is a chemical interaction of the environment?
xs: The environment's **chemical interactions** include the **carbon** and **nitrogen cycles**.
73.x: The environment's chemical interactions include the carbon and nitrogen cycles.

73.s: Nutrients, water and air form which component of the environment?
xs: **nutrients, water and air** form the **physical** component; the **biological** component is the **organisms**.
73.x: nutrients, water and air form the physical component; the biological component is the organisms.

73.s: The environment, as the surroundings in which organisms live, is best described as?
xs: The environment is the **surroundings and conditions** in which organisms live, and it is **never static**.
73.x: The environment is the surroundings and conditions in which organisms live, and it is never static.

73.s: Microbes belong to which category of the environment?
xs: **Microbes** belong to the **biotic** category (plants, animals, microbes).
73.x: Microbes belong to the biotic category (plants, animals, microbes).

73.s: Which belongs to the physical category of the environment?
xs: The physical category is **lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere**
73.x: The physical category is lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere

73.s: Which of the following is included in the cultural category of the environment?
73.x: The cultural environment is man-made and includes social, economic and political aspects.
xs: **Political institutions** fall in the **cultural** (man-made) category — option **(2)**.
Cultural = **social, economic, political**; wild animals are **biotic**; atmospheric gases and soil minerals are **physical**.
xa: Physical = **lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere**.
Biotic = **plants, animals, microbes**.
Functions: resources, **assimilating wastes**, habitat for biodiversity.
73.tq: Identify the man-made category rather than a natural component.

73.s: Which always contains life?
Which may exist even in the absence of life?
xs: An **environment may not have life** — correct.
73.x: An environment may not have life — correct.

73.s: Which one of the following is NOT a primary function of the environment?
73.x: The primary functions of the environment are providing resources, assimilating wastes and serving as a habitat for biodiversity. Generating synthetic chemicals is not one of them (APPSC 2024 trap).
xs: **Generating synthetic chemicals** is NOT a function — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2024** trap).
The primary functions: **provide resources**, **assimilate wastes**, **habitat for biodiversity**.
xa: Environment includes **physical**, **biotic** and **cultural** categories.
Environment is **never static**.
73.tq: Resources, waste assimilation, habitat - synthetic chemicals is the odd one out.

73.s: All populations of different species living in an area form a?
xs: A **community** = all populations of **different species** in an area — correct.
xa: Order: **organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere**.
73.x: A community = all populations of different species in an area — correct.

73.s: A biome is chiefly defined by?
xs: A **biome** is defined by **climate and dominant vegetation** (rainforest, tundra, desert) — wrong; density and sex ratio are **population** attributes.
73.x: A biome is defined by climate and dominant vegetation (rainforest, tundra, desert) — wrong; density and sex ratio are population attributes.

73.s: Which one of the following represents the correct ecological order from the smallest to the largest level?
o: Organism → community → population → ecosystem → biome → biosphere
Organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere
Population → organism → community → biome → ecosystem → biosphere
Organism → ecosystem → population → community → biome → biosphere
73.x: The ecological order is organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome and biosphere.
xs: Order: **organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere** — option **(2)**.
The others misplace community/population or ecosystem/biome.
xa: Full chain starts with **atoms → molecules → protoplasm → cells**.
"Ecology" was coined by **Ernst Haeckel (1869)**.
The **ecosystem** is the **basic functional unit of ecology**.
73.tq: Check the hierarchy sequentially from the individual level upward.

73.s: Fungal and bacterial spores above which altitude are dormant?
xs: Spores above **8,000 m** are **dormant** — correct.
73.x: Spores above 8,000 m are dormant — correct.

73.s: From where does energy enter the biosphere?
xs: Energy comes from the **sun**; nutrients are **recycled within** — correct.
73.x: Energy comes from the sun; nutrients are recycled within — correct.

73.s: Where is the biosphere absent?
o: Poles, highest peaks and deepest oceans
xs: Absent at the poles, highest peaks and deepest oceans
73.x: Absent at the poles, highest peaks and deepest oceans

73.s: How are habitats related to environments?
xs: **all habitats are environments** — correct.
73.x: all habitats are environments — correct.

73.s: How many species can one habitat contain?
xs: **one habitat can hold many species** — correct.
73.x: one habitat can hold many species — correct.

73.s: The fundamental niche of a species refers to
o: the actual range occupied after competition
the full range of conditions and resources it could use in the absence of other species
73.x: Fundamental niche is the potential range of conditions and resources available to a species when competition and other biological limitations are absent.
xs: The **fundamental niche** is the full range of conditions and resources a species could use **free from other species** — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2021**).
The range actually used under competition is the **realised niche** — option (1).
xa: **Niche breadth**: **specialists** (koala — eucalyptus) vs **generalists**.
**Hutchinson** gave the **n-dimensional niche** (**1957**).
Niche is **unique to each species**.
73.tq: Distinguish potential range from actual range.

73.s: Who proposed the habitat niche concept in 1917?
xs: **Grinnell**: The **niche** concept
73.x: Grinnell: The niche concept

73.s: Who proposed the functional niche concept in 1927?
xs: **Elton** = **functional niche** (**1927**); **Hutchinson** = **n-dimensional niche** (**1957**).
xa: Elton also wrote **Animal Ecology** and described the **pyramid of numbers**.
73.x: Elton = functional niche (1927); Hutchinson = n-dimensional niche (1957).

73.s: Who proposed the n-dimensional niche concept?
xs: **Elton** = **functional niche** (**1927**); **Hutchinson** = **n-dimensional niche** (**1957**).
73.x: Elton = functional niche (1927); Hutchinson = n-dimensional niche (1957).

73.s: A koala, which feeds mainly on eucalyptus, is best described as a
73.x: A specialist uses a narrow range of resources. Dependence of the koala mainly on eucalyptus is an example of narrow niche breadth.
xs: The koala, eating only **eucalyptus**, is a **specialist** with **narrow niche breadth** — option **(2)**.
**Generalists** (most animals) have broad niche breadth.
xa: **Fundamental niche** = range possible without other species; **realised niche** = range used under competition.
No two species occupy the **same niche**.
73.tq: Infer niche breadth from the range of resources used.

73.s: The functional role of a species in its habitat is called its?
xs: A niche is the **functional role** ("profession") of a species — correct.
xa: Niche is set by habitat, food, reproduction and physical-chemical factors.
A niche is **unique to each species** — correct.
73.x: A niche is the functional role ("profession") of a species — correct.

73.s: How many species can occupy exactly the same niche?
xs: One habitat can hold many species
73.x: One habitat can hold many species

73.s: Which of the following is NOT a population attribute?
73.x: Density, mortality, age structure and sex ratio are population attributes. Dominant vegetation is associated with the description of a biome.
xs: **Dominant vegetation** is not a population attribute — option **(2)**; it defines a **biome**.
**Mortality**, **density** and **age structure** are population attributes (with **sex ratio**, **natality**).
xa: **J-curve** = exponential growth (dN/dt = rN).

73.s: Population density is measured as?

73.x: Individuals per unit area is correct

73.s: Mortality in a population refers to?
xs: **Mortality** = deaths per unit time; **natality** = births (individuals per female per unit time).
73.x: Mortality = deaths per unit time; natality = births (individuals per female per unit time).

73.s: Natality in a population refers to?
xs: **Mortality** = deaths per unit time; **natality** = births (individuals per female per unit time).
73.x: Mortality = deaths per unit time; natality = births (individuals per female per unit time).

73.s: A triangular age pyramid indicates which kind of population?
xs: Expanding** population is correct
73.x: Expanding population is correct

73.s: A bell-shaped age pyramid indicates which kind of population?
xs: **Bell** = **stable**; **urn** = **declining**.

73.s: An urn-shaped age pyramid indicates which kind of population?
xs: **Bell** = **stable**; **urn** = **declining**.
73.x: Bell = stable; urn = declining.

73.s: Which growth curve shows logistic growth levelling off at carrying capacity?
The maximum population an environment can sustain is called its?
xs: **carrying capacity** is the **maximum sustainable population**.

73.s: A J-shaped population curve shows which type of growth?
xs: The **J-curve** is **exponential growth** with **unlimited resources** (dN/dt = rN); it does not level off.

73.s: Insects and weeds commonly show which life strategy?

73.s: Elephants and humans commonly show which life strategy?
xs: **elephants, humans** are **K-selected** — correct.

o: Many small offspring with little care

73.x: Ecosystems are open for energy and matter;

73.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the basic functional unit of ecology?
73.x: The ecosystem - a biotic community plus its non-living surroundings linked by energy flow and nutrient cycling - is the basic functional unit of ecology (APPSC PYQ). A population is one species in an area; a biome is a large climatic-vegetation region; the biosphere is the sum of all ecosystems.
xs: The **ecosystem** is the **basic functional unit of ecology** (APPSC PYQ) — option **(3)**.

xa: Term coined by **Tansley**, **1935**.

73.s: An abiotic factor is best defined as which one of the following?
o: An organism that obtains food from dead organic matter
Any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment
A living component occupying the highest trophic level
A biological interaction between two species

xs: An **abiotic factor** is **any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment** (**APPSC 2018**) — option **(2)**.
Feeding on dead matter = **saprotrophs**; species interactions are biotic.
xa: Types: **climatic**, **edaphic** (soil), **topographic**.

73.s: Light, temperature and rainfall are which type of abiotic factors?

73.s: Soil texture, pH and minerals are which type of abiotic factors?

87.s: In-situ conservation is generally considered the most effective method because it:
o: Eliminates the need for protected areas
Can conserve only genetic material and not living species
Keeps species interacting with their environment

xs: Disaster risk is expressed as **Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity** — option **(1)**.
Risk rises with **hazard** and **vulnerability** and falls as **capacity** (strengths/resources to cope) rises, so capacity belongs in the **denominator**.
The other formulas put capacity in the numerator or drop vulnerability, reversing this logic.
xa: **Risk** = probability of harm from the **hazard-vulnerability interaction**.
**Vulnerability** dimensions: **physical, social, economic, environmental**.
**DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).
106.tq: Capacity divides risk; vulnerability multiplies it.

**Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.
